The Squid Game cookie recipe took the internet by storm after the release of the Squid Game Netflix series, turning a humble Korean street candy into one of the most talked-about viral food challenges in modern pop culture. Known traditionally as dalgona candy, this simple yet dramatic sweet became globally famous as the Squid Game honeycomb cookie, captivating viewers with its intense challenge and minimalist ingredients.

In this guide, we’ll explore everything you need to know about the Squid Game cookie recipe, from its cultural roots in Korean cuisine and South Korean candy traditions to detailed candy making technique, shaping methods, safety tips, and party uses. This is not just a recipe—it’s a complete informational resource about the Netflix Squid Game cookie, also called Korean dalgona candy, honeycomb toffee cookie, dalgona biscuit, and Korean sugar cookie.

 What Is the Squid Game Cookie?

The Squid Game cookie recipe is based on a traditional Korean dalgona candy recipe. The candy is made by melting sugar over low heat cooking, adding a small amount of baking soda, and shaping it into thin discs with stamped symbols.

 The Traditional Roots of Dalgona Candy

The Squid Game cookie is a traditional Korean dalgona candy made with melted sugar and baking soda. This South Korean candy has been sold for decades as part of Korean street food culture, especially near schools. Vendors often challenged kids to carve shapes without breaking the candy, offering a free treat if they succeeded.

 Is Dalgona Candy the Same as Squid Game Cookie?

Yes. Is dalgona candy the same as Squid Game cookie?
Absolutely. The Squid Game cookies, dalgona candy recipe, Squid Game honeycomb cookie, and honeycomb sugar candy all refer to the same Korean sugar cookie, just popularized under a new name by Netflix food trends.

 Why the Squid Game Cookie Became a Viral Netflix Dessert

The rise of the viral Netflix dessert is directly linked to K-drama food trends and the intense scene in the Squid Game Netflix series.

 The Squid Game Challenge Cookie Explained

The Squid Game challenge cookie involved contestants carving stamped candy shapes without cracking the brittle surface.

The Squid Game cookie challenge involves carefully carving shapes without breaking the candy.

This dramatic moment introduced millions to viral dessert ideas, edible game challenges, and fun dessert recipes.

 Ingredients Used in Squid Game Cookies

One of the reasons the easy Squid Game cookie recipe became so popular is its simplicity.

 Minimalist Ingredient Recipe List

This is a minimalist ingredient recipe, making it perfect as a budget dessert recipe, vegan candy recipe, egg-free dessert, dairy-free dessert, and gluten-free candy.

Ingredients:

  • Sugar

  • White sugar

  • Granulated sugar

  • Baking soda

  • Water

  • Oil (for greasing)

  • Parchment paper

  • Nonstick surface

No flour, no eggs, no butter—just pure caramel magic.

 Tools Needed for Making Squid Game Honeycomb Cookies

Even though the ingredients are simple, proper tools make a difference.

 Essential Candy-Making Tools

  • Ladle

  • Metal spoon

  • Nonstick pan

  • Saucepan

  • Spatula

  • Cookie cutter

  • Needle tool

  • Toothpick

  • Parchment paper

  • Silicone mat

These tools help with stovetop cooking, pouring hot sugar, and shaping cookies safely.

 Candy Making Technique – How Dalgona Is Made

Understanding the candy making technique is crucial for success.

 Step-by-Step Cooking Method (Informational)

  1. Melting sugar slowly in a nonstick pan

  2. Caramelizing sugar using low heat cooking

  3. Stirring sugar gently with a metal spoon

  4. Adding baking soda once fully melted

  5. Whipping sugar foam quickly

  6. Pouring hot sugar onto a nonstick surface

  7. Flattening candy with a ladle

  8. Shaping cookies using cutters

  9. Cooling candy completely

 Why Does Dalgona Candy Need Baking Soda?

Dalgona candy becomes light and crispy when baking soda is added to caramelized sugar. The reaction creates air bubbles, giving it a honeycomb toffee cookie texture.

 Shapes and Symbols in Squid Game Cookies

The shapes are what make the Netflix Squid Game cookie iconic.

 Classic Squid Game Symbols

  • Circle shape

  • Triangle shape

  • Star shape

  • Umbrella shape

These Squid Game symbols are pressed into the candy using cookie cutters, forming stamped candy shapes and carved cookie designs.

 Texture Variations – Crispy vs Chewy

 Crispy Dalgona Candy

  • Thin pouring

  • Quick cooling

  • Results in crispy dalgona candy

 Chewy Dalgona Candy

  • Slightly thicker candy

  • Less aeration

  • Results in chewy dalgona candy

Both textures fall under crunchy caramel candy styles.

 Is the Squid Game Cookie Hard to Make?

Are Squid Game cookies hard to make?
Not really. This is a beginner dalgona recipe, but precision matters. Temperature control and timing are key.

 Common Mistakes

  • Overheating sugar

  • Too much baking soda

  • Pouring too slowly

These can lead to cracked candy or bitterness.

 Safety and Edibility Concerns

 Is Dalgona Candy Safe to Eat?

Is dalgona candy safe to eat?
Yes, when made correctly. However, pouring hot sugar requires caution, especially for children.

 Can Kids Make Dalgona Candy?

Can kids make dalgona candy?
Kids can help with shaping cookies and carving, but adults should handle stovetop cooking.

 Why Did the Cookie Break in Squid Game?

Why did the cookie break in Squid Game?
Because the honeycomb sugar candy is brittle. Thin edges and poor carving technique cause fractures.

 How to Make Squid Game Cookies at Home

How do you make Squid Game cookies at home?
By following the authentic dalgona candy process using basic tools, minimal ingredients, and patience.

 No-Mold Dalgona Cookie Method

The no-mold dalgona cookie approach uses cutters instead of molds, making it easier for home kitchens.

 Final Thoughts on the Squid Game Cookie Recipe

The Squid Game cookie recipe is more than just a sweet it’s a cultural phenomenon, a viral Netflix dessert, and a perfect example of how street food sweets can become global icons. With its roots in Korean street food, minimalist ingredients, and unforgettable challenge, this honeycomb sugar candy remains one of the most recognizable Netflix food trends of all time.
